chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allāh informed me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him saying: If I were to have a nosebleed enough to fill a vessel, I would do no more than wipe the blood from myself and perform salat (prayer).

key_terms.دَوْرَقًا: a vessel or jug, used here to indicate a large amount

ai.seo_question: Does a nosebleed invalidate salat (prayer) or require renewing wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that a nosebleed does not require more than wiping away the blood before performing salat (prayer). Its significance is in the jurisprudential ruling on ritual purity and the effect of nosebleeding on worship.
